Synopsis:
French consumer confidence is deteriorating sharply ahead of the April/May 2027 presidential election. Households are cutting discretionary spending across restaurants, clothing, travel and leisure, pressured by inflation, high energy prices and fiscal uncertainty. Consumer spending — half of French GDP — is weakening despite households drawing down savings to sustain it. Purchasing power (real disposable income) fell 0.5% in Q2. The political backdrop features competing fiscal proposals from presidential candidates (VAT cuts, wage hikes, payroll tax relief), but economists warn France's constrained public finances leave little room to support households. The risk of a consumer-led slowdown or mild recession is rising.
